headline: JPMorgan strategists say a Democratic sweep of Congress in November could hurt AI data center stocks, which now make up about 45% of the S&P 500.
score_reason: Strategist note read through a personal-finance site; midterm outcome is a forecast. No reduction.
importance_line: People whose retirement savings track the S&P 500 are exposed to AI shares, and the note ties their prospects to US election results; the outcome is a prediction market estimate, not a fact.
summary: Moneywise, in a version carried by Yahoo Finance, reports that JPMorgan strategist Dubravko Lakos-Bujas wrote that Republican control of Congress would likely give AI infrastructure the most supportive federal policy backdrop, and that a "blue wave" (Democrats winning the House and Senate), which Polymarket puts at 85%, could hurt data center stocks. The article says AI stocks make up 45% of the S&P 500 by market value and that data centers have become a political issue with voters.
notes: Original is Moneywise; text read on Yahoo Finance. The 45% figure is the article's own.
